items.markdown:
Yes. I’d look for a **Staffordshire Bull Terrier (Staffy) breeder rather than choosing primarily on the blue colour**. Blue is an accepted Staffordshire Bull Terrier colour under the Royal Kennel Club standard, but the Kennel Club specifically says health and temperament should take priority over colour. [Royal Kennel Club](https://www.royalkennelclub.com/search/breeds-a-to-z/breeds/terrier/staffordshire-bull-terrier/?utm_source=chatgpt.com) 

### Where to look near South Yorkshire

- **Blue staffy** — a dog breeder returned in the South Yorkshire-area search. I’d treat this as a lead to investigate, rather than an endorsement; ask for the parents' health-test certificates before arranging a deposit.
- The **Royal Kennel Club's Find a Puppy** service is another useful starting point. It lets you search for Staffordshire Bull Terrier litters by location and filter for puppies whose parents have been health tested. [Royal Kennel Club](https://www.royalkennelclub.com/search/find-a-puppy/?ActiveCertifiedBreeder=False&Breeds=Staffordshire+Bull+Terrier&Distance=15&FemaleDogs=False&GeneralRescueClubs=False&HealthTested=False&MaleDogs=False&SearchRescueClubs=False&SortNearest=False&TotalResults=0&utm_source=chatgpt.com)
- Current marketplace listings also show blue Staffies advertised in/around South Yorkshire, but I'd use these mainly to identify breeders and then independently verify their health testing and breeding practices. [Staffie-Owners.co.uk](https://www.staffie-owners.co.uk/staffies-for-sale/south-yorkshire?colour=blue&kc_registered=yes&ready_to_leave=now&sex=male&utm_source=chatgpt.com)

### What I'd ask the breeder

Send something along these lines:

>  **“Could you please send me the registered names/numbers of both parents and copies of their health-test results? Specifically, have both parents been DNA tested for L-2-HGA and hereditary cataracts (HC-HSF4), and have they had their eyes and elbows tested? I'd also like to know the parents' temperaments, whether I can meet the mother with the puppies, and what socialisation the puppies have had.”**
Those questions matter because the Royal Kennel Club's current Staffordshire Bull Terrier health recommendations include **L-2-HGA and hereditary-cataract DNA testing, elbow testing, and eye testing including litter screening**. [Royal Kennel Club](https://www.royalkennelclub.com/search/breeds-a-to-z/breeds/terrier/staffordshire-bull-terrier/?utm_source=chatgpt.com) [Royal Kennel Club](https://www.royalkennelclub.com/BreedSpecificRequirements?utm_source=chatgpt.com) 

Also ask:

- **Can I see the puppies with their mother at the breeder's home?**
- **Can I see the original health certificates rather than just being told they're “health tested”?**
- What are the **registered names and KC numbers** of mum and dad?
- What is the parents' **inbreeding coefficient**?
- Have the puppies had **litter eye screening**?
- Have they been microchipped, vaccinated and wormed?
- What food are they currently eating?
- How have they been socialised to people, household noises, handling and other dogs?
- What paperwork comes with the puppy, and is there a **puppy contract**?
- Will the breeder take the dog back or help rehome it if circumstances change?

A particularly important point: **“health checked by a vet” isn't the same thing as breed-specific genetic and screening tests.** For L-2-HGA, for example, a carrier is normally healthy but can pass the mutation on, so you want to understand the actual results for *both* parents. [Royal Kennel Club](https://www.royalkennelclub.com/health-and-dog-care/health-dog-care/health/getting-started-with-health-testing-and-screening/dna-testing/dna-test-l-2hga/?utm_source=chatgpt.com) 

### Red flags

I'd walk away if the breeder:

- won't let you see the mother with the litter;
- won't show actual health-test documentation;
- wants a deposit before you've visited;
- has lots of different breeds/litters available;
- is heavily focused on “rare”, “exclusive” or exaggerated blue/pocket/XL-type marketing;
- can't tell you the parents' registered names;
- wants the puppy to leave before **8 weeks**;
- is unwilling to answer questions about what happens if you can no longer keep the dog.

If you tell me **how far you're willing to travel from South Yorkshire (e.g. 30, 60 or 100 miles)** and whether you want **KC-registered only**, I can search current listings and breeder directories and narrow it down to specific breeders/litters to investigate.
